Headers: the fetch tool presents a browser-like client and cannot send custom headers, so whether each feed accepts the watch's user agent 'lifesavinglab-watch/1.0' is untested from here; none of the five confirmed feeds needed anything special for the fetch tool.
notes: Outcome: four of the ten named services have a confirmed feed (Canadian Coast Guard, Maritime New Zealand, Redningsselskapet via NTB Kommunikasjon, KNRM with two feeds), plus one working fallback from a state body (Surf Life Saving NSW) that is not one of the named ten; hence 'partial'. Every address in rows was fetched on 2026-10-21 and returned items; dates and feed titles are quoted in evidence. Content kinds: Canadian Coast Guard = government news releases (announcements, not incidents); Maritime NZ = news and media releases (safety campaigns and rules); Redningsselskapet = press releases, including monthly drowning counts ('Ni personer druknet i september'); KNRM Reddingrapporten = incident log of written rescue reports (newest 17 Oct 2026); KNRM Nieuws = organisational news; SLS NSW = news and media releases. For the watch, the KNRM Reddingrapporten feed and the Redningsselskapet feed are the most useful; the Canadian feed will rarely match the watch's keywords. Terms of use found: canada.ca allows non-commercial reproduction; Maritime NZ allows personal-use reproduction with acknowledgement; KNRM's disclaimer reserves all reproduction except personal use; NTB and SLS NSW state none. None of them mentions RSS or automated reading; since the watch stores only links, dates, a derived kind and a headline hash, none of these terms appears to be a barrier, but a person should decide. Robots: knrm.nl, maritimenz.govt.nz, api.io.canada.ca, kommunikasjon.ntb.no and surflifesaving.com.au were all readable by the fetch tool, which respects robots.txt; ntbinfo.no and salvamentomaritimo.es were not. Not found: SLSA (sls.com.au errors on every address), Royal Life Saving Australia (no feed on a Squiz site; newsletter only), DGzRS (TYPO3 site, newsletter only), Irish Coast Guard (gov.ie has no feeds), Salvamento Marítimo (host unreadable from here), Guardia Costiera (host unreadable from here). Two caveats for whoever enables these in watch/sources.json: the KNRM Nieuws feed carries a future-dated agenda item (2027) as its first item, and the fetch tool flagged instruction-like text inside one KNRM Nieuws item description, so the watch should keep ignoring descriptions. The Canadian feed's dates are 'updated' timestamps, not 'published'. No repository file was modified.
